status: Preserved original engine and modern SDL2 reimplementation for unfinished Ermentrud; independent builds/playability unverified
notes: Ermentrud / Inga is one adventure-game/engine lineage spanning the preserved native AmigaOS3 engine and the modern Inga SDL reimplementation. README says Ermentrud and original Inga were created in 2001–2004 and the game was never finished. That origin does not date the later reimplementation. The original C engine has graphics, animation, actors, inventory, dialogues, bytecode execution and audio; the modern code has game state, navigation, scripts, scenes, menus and sound. inga-sdl is the canonical tracked root; inga-amigaos3 is an original-engine source alias, not a second project. This subject includes an original Amiga game-engine source archive plus a substantive modern reimplementation and native modern Amiga-family ports. The author explicitly chose a complete rewrite of important engine features instead of mechanically replacing Amiga calls, while retaining the old data formats and interpreter lineage. It is not a disassembly or a claim of extracted original machine code. Ermentrud remains an unfinished game; author compatibility/release descriptions do not verify completion or playability here. The preserved original AmigaOS3 engine is an actual 68k C-source lineage. Makefile.vbcc selects vc +aos68k and -cpu=68020; the original GCC options select m68020-60/soft-float/noixemul. source_cpu records 68020 for that concrete preserved engine configuration, not an assumed minimum derived solely from the Amiga brand. Original source is C rather than machine code. The original-engine build directly selects 68020. Modern Makefile.mos uses ppc-morphos-gcc-10; Makefile.amigaos4 is an AmigaOS4/newlib/SDL2 recipe, forming the documented PowerPC port lineage. README gives a CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 Xcode example. These establish 68020, PowerPC and ARM64 selected targets. Reviewed generic Linux/Windows CMake instructions do not establish a complete host ISA matrix or additional minima. The original engine has GCC and VBCC build recipes; VBCC selects +aos68k -cpu=68020. Modern CMake requires >=3.16.3 and SDL2, SDL2_mixer and SDL2_ttf; documented platform recipes additionally specify their SDK/dependencies. notes: NT Virtual CP/M Machine is a standalone C++ command-line runner for CP/M .COM tools. ntvcm.cxx loads a selected host file at guest 0x100, creates CP/M entry hooks and enters x80.cxx. README documents asm/load, Turbo Pascal, Aztec C, WordStar and many other tools; they are compatibility examples, not separately reconstructed projects. The current head has removed the former GDB/MI debugger-host mode, so it is not advertised as a current capability. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: be598f65c1b649f5250dcd6d8fef266b1b86413e. An emulator with native CP/M BDOS/file and console translation, an 8080/Z80 trace disassembler and optional per-PC CSV profiling. It executes original instructions and synthesizes BDOS/BIOS hooks rather than booting a CP/M disk or requiring an original ROM. Host fopen/fread/fwrite implement FCB file operations. Original guest tools must be supplied with their own overlays/data; this record is the runner, not a full disk/hardware emulator or compiler reconstruction. x80.cxx and README explicitly implement Z80 with optional -8 8080 mode, making both guest source ISAs. CP/M 2.2 is the main guest API, supplemented by selected CP/M 3 and nonstandard services. README excludes BIOS disk-layout access, undocumented 8080 instructions and precise cycle accuracy. Recent commits distinguish optional Z80 R/MEMPTR accuracy and unattached I/O gaps; upstream validation reports do not establish universal instruction/hardware compatibility. msvcenv.bat explicitly selects Windows x86, x64 and ARM64 native toolchains. README documents a RISC-V Linux output runnable under RVOS and a real-mode DOS Watcom output; mwatcom.bat uses -0 with the DOS target, grounding 8086. Canonical target labels refer to these host executables, while source 8080/Z80 remains separate. RVOS’s AMD64/ARM32/etc host list does not automatically prove native ntvcm ports on every such system. Linux/macOS recipes do not establish an exhaustive ISA matrix. Native MSVC/g++ recipes and the Watcom real-mode DOS route are present. Unix release scripts default to RSS disabled; enabling RSS introduces cpp-httplib/OpenSSL dependencies, and README reports unresolved macOS RSS-enabled builds. Windows mr.bat enables RSS. A pinned-head Windows-2022 MSVC CI run succeeded and archived ntvcm.exe; the workflow contains no guest-test step. These observed upstream build results remain separate from maintainer CPU-test claims and this unrun review. All four build flags remain null: compilation, execution, gameplay and byte-equivalence are independently unverified. The real-mode DOS output and explicit host toolchain choices are preserved in target fields, but no numeric RAM or supported minimum DOS/Windows/macOS/Linux version is established. Guest 64 KiB layout, 80x24 console mode and emulated MHz are not host memory/CPU minima. runtime_profiles stays empty.
